This is Hiplet. 21st century (coined 2009).

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Created by Homer Hans Bryant at the Chicago Multi-Cultural Dance Center (CMDC), Hiplet traces back to Bryant's 1992 "Rap Ballet" (also cited as 1994).
The term "Hiplet" was coined in 2009.
The style gained international prominence in May 2016 through viral Instagram videos, leading to appearances on ABC News, Good Morning America, and TEDx.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Hiplet serves as a contemporary vehicle for dancers of color—predominantly young Black dancers between 12 and 16 years old—to engage with pointe work while expressing their urban culture and personal identity within a field that historically lacked diversity.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Hiplet- When Ballet Meets Hip-Hop.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f5/Hiplet-_When_Ballet_Meets_Hip-Hop.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Hiplet pairs rigorous ballet pointe technique with hip-hop and African dance movement.
Dancers employ traditional pointe shoes to perform sharp angles, off-balance shifts, and fluid torso dynamics.
Solid classical technique developed over years of practice is required to execute the style safely.
Watch for Pointe hip isolation, Off-center relevé.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Flexible, including studio formations, ensemble stage arrangements, and camera-facing broadcast framing

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Hiplet replaces classical orchestral music with urban music, hip-hop, and pop tracks.
The movement accents syncopated rhythms, heavy basslines, and modern musical beats.
Listen for the Electronic drum machines, Synthesizers, Bass beats.
The pulse is 4/4.
Urban music and hip-hop beats characterized by heavy electronic basslines, rhythmic drum sequences, and contemporary pop production, replacing traditional ballet accompaniment.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear traditional ballet attire, including leotards, tights, and hair buns.
A defining element is that dancers of color dye their tights and pointe shoes to match their skin tones.
Settings range from dance studios and television studios to public stages and digital video platforms.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Homer Hans Bryant is the founder of the Chicago Multi-Cultural Dance Center and creator of Hiplet.
Professional ballet dancer Misty Copeland is also associated with Bryant's advocacy for Black dancers in classical ballet.

Evolved from classical ballet and hip-hop/African dance fusions, drawing a direct lineage from Homer Hans Bryant's 1992/1994 "Rap Ballet" to the formal coining of Hiplet in 2009 at the Chicago Multi-Cultural Dance Center.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Hiplet is parent of Ballet: Provides the core technical foundation and en pointe execution required for Hiplet.
Hiplet is parent of Hip-hop dance: Provides the rhythmic structure, hip/torso isolations, and sharp movement angles.
